messages:
support_jay: Customer Alan (ACME) reports large spike at 09:10 UTC — requests queued, 429s for a minute, then slow ramp. He sees errors like 'attach timeout' and a lot of warmup logs. He pasted repro steps. Can someone triage? :loudspeaker:

customer_alan: Repro steps I ran: 1) send 500 concurrent requests with burst=100 2) model=redwood/base-7B 3) region=us-west-2. We saw 15-25s tail latencies and a few 429s. Tokens count ~60.

maria: looking. Do we have the Dedicated pool id and the min/max for that account?

support_jay: pool id: ded-az-7, minReplicas=1, maxReplicas=6, reserved=true. Customer is on a reserved plan.

ops-bot: [autoscaler] scale-request: desired=4 current=1 pending_provision=3 reason=burst_probe_concurrency timestamp=2026-03-17T09:10:34Z

chen: Quick guess: autoscaler issued provisioning but K8s attach step stuck on image pull / pod init. Can you grab the pod events from the node where the new pods scheduled?

maria: I grabbed node events — image pullretry and registry 429s for the model container. Looks like container registry throttling is delaying startup. Also some nodes reported GPU scheduling delay (NVIDIA driver busy) right after the burst.

chen: That matches. Two compounding issues: registry backoff -> delayed pod readiness, and noisy neighbor causing GPU allocation delay. Both slow the scale path. We should confirm if warm pool had any healthy spare pods.

support_jay: Customer says warm pool was set to 0 for cost reasons. They relied on minReplicas=1 only.

maria: ah. With minReplicas=1 and warm_pool=0, burstiness will force cold scheduling. Recommend warm_pool >= 2 for this workload. Also adding imagePullPolicy=IfNotPresent and regional mirror could help.

chen: Repro commands I ran in staging to validate:
```
# simulate customer burst
siege -c500 -t1M --content-type "application/json" 'POST http://dedicated-host/api/generate'
```
Observations: new pods created, but 60% of provision time spent in imagePull backoff. Once images present, scale <1s per replica.

eva: Noted. Ops suggestion for mitigation: 1) set warm_pool=2, 2) pre-pull container image on node pool via DaemonSet (short term), 3) set attach timeout higher to avoid premature 429s, 4) surface registry quota to customer if pulling from their registry.

support_jay: Customer asked for a short-term workaround they can apply themselves — they prefer not to change warm_pool. Any minimal change?

chen: If they won't increase warm_pool, easiest is to switch to a mirrored image hosted on our registry (we can serve cached images) — that cuts image pull time. Also set request hedging on the probe (probe retries faster).

maria: Leaving note: create internal alert when imagePullBackoff spikes > 5% of scale operations and when gpu-sched-delay detected. That will catch future noisy-neighbor races.

support_jay: I sent customer steps: (1) enable mirror image (we can help), (2) temporarily increase attach timeout to 90s, (3) consider warm_pool=2. They accepted mirror + timeout change.

ops-bot: [action] ticket/7892 assigned to eng-platform for registry mirroring and autoscaler probe tuning.

chen: Follow-up: We'll also look at autoscaler backoff config — it currently waits exponential backoff on pod failures; maybe aggressive probe for burst policy. I'll open PR for probe tuning and docs on recommended warm_pool defaults for bursty workloads.

maria: Closing loop — once mirror rolled, customer reported tail latencies drop to <3s and no 429s on a second test. Marking as mitigated. :white_check_mark:

support_jay: Thanks team — will update customer and close the escalation.
